summary: Feed s137_double is degraded: 17.9% of TCP sessions are one-way (exceeds 10% threshold) and 78% of bytes are encrypted (exceeds 60% IDS tolerance), limiting bidirectional stateful inspection and payload visibility.

findings.root_cause: Asymmetric visibility - packet broker is forwarding only one direction for many TCP sessions. Likely SPAN/TAP inputs from opposite sides of the flow are not aggregated to the same IDS tool port, or asymmetric routing is captured on a single link only.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions for TCP stream reassembly and stateful signature detection. One-way sessions cause broken flows, missed exploits, and high false-negative rate.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS port so the IDS sees complete bidirectional sessions for accurate reassembly and detection.

findings.root_cause: 78% of traffic is TLS/encrypted and delivered to IDS without prior decryption. IDS needs full cleartext payload but receives opaque encrypted streams.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot inspect encrypted payloads - signatures and anomaly detection are blind beyond headers/metadata, reducing detection coverage well below expected 60% encrypted tolerance.

recommended_fix.why: Provide decrypted copy or selectively decrypt policy-relevant TLS at packet broker/SSL visibility layer before IDS so IDS regains payload inspection while respecting privacy policy.
